newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat ends mostly lower as spread unwinds.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat ends mostly lower as spread unwinds.

text.p: Unwinding of bull spreads and profit taking of the December/March spread pressed CBOT wheat futures to a mostly lower close, traders said.
"There was a lot of unwinding of the bull spreads getting ready for first notice day. There was a lot of profit taking of the spreads," said Vic Lespinasse of Dean Witter Reynolds.

First notice day for delivery on the Dec is slated for Friday and as of late Tuesday 3,682,652 bushels of wheat in Toledo had been registered and 20,202 in Chicago. Registration means that the commodity is eligible for delivery, but will not necessarily be delivered.
The consensus is that wheat deliveries will be light to nil but there was scattered talk that some wheat may be posted for delivery.
"There was talk we may see some wheat delivered," said Ron Kucha of O'Connor and Co.
An early drop in the Dow industrial stock index was unnerving to some potential longs, traders said.
"People are keeping an eye on the stock market. If it breaks further that may hit down here," said Ron Kucha said.
Wheat closed 2-3/4 cents per bushel lower to 3/4 higher, with December down 2-3/4 at $4.13.
The Dow fell 50 points early, triggering index-arbitrage trading curbs on the New York Stock Exchange before early losses were partly recouped. At 1441 CST was trading at 6541.83, down 5.96 points.
December dropped relative to the March because the December/March recently widened to a steep 25 cent per bushel difference, premium the December.
Tight nearby stocks, firm cash basis markets plus increased optimism about export sales of U.S. wheat had boosted the December relative to the March, the traders said.

FIMAT Futures bear spread three million bushels of the May/December at 46 to 50 cents per bushel, premium December, traders said. E.D. and F. Man International spread nearly two million bushels of December/March at 25 cents, premium December, they said.

Volume was thin and commercial selling contributed to the losses, they said. Cargill sold two million bushels of March which sparked the break from the day's highs which were set near the open. Term Commodities, the marketing arm of Louis Dreyfus Corp, sold one million bushels of March, traders said.
Short term technical indicators showed the market was into overbought territory, sources said.

The daily nine day relative strength index (RSI) for December closed Monday at 69 points. The market generally views an RSI of 70 or more as an overbought market. The RSI for December Tuesday closed at 66.6 points.
Longer-term indicators continue to give off supportive signals with the four- and 20-day moving averages for the December through May showing bullish flags early Tuesday.
Support levels in the December were at $4.11-1/2 for first support and $4.02 was the second support area. The session low for December was $4.06-1/2.
Wheat futures volume was estimated at 18,000 contracts below the 19,827 traded Monday, according to the CBOT.
In wheat options, Tenco Inc sold 50 March $4.40 calls at 4-1/2 cents and Goldenberg Hehmeyer sold 50 March $4.00 calls at 13 cents, traders said.
Wheat options volume was estimated at 4,800 contracts, below the 5,229 traded Monday.
